narrative.title: Why Psychiatry, Why AbbVie
narrative.body:
I spent the first part of my career in institutional finance, most recently at Goldman Sachs. The real skill wasn't the numbers. It was earning trust from busy clients and learning complex contracts well enough to solve problems for them. In 2023, I left to become a full-time parent.

In 2025, I watched a stranger save someone's life during a medical emergency. It pushed me to become an EMT. During my ER clinicals, I saw psychiatric patients in two very different situations: people whose suffering was primarily psychiatric, and people whose physical emergencies were connected to an untreated psychiatric condition. My reasons for wanting this work are personal. People I love have struggled with mental illness, and I know the helplessness of watching it. I've seen what the right medication and advocacy can do. I've also seen what happens when people don't get either: isolation, instability, and sometimes suicide.

Vraylar immediately stood out to me because of its role in AbbVie's psychiatry portfolio and the patients it serves. I've spent time learning its mechanism of action, clinical positioning, and the broader psychiatry pipeline, including bretisilocin and ABBV-932.

I know this market. I've lived in Prosper for the past few years, and I've watched the DFW suburbs grow rapidly. That growth makes access to psychiatric care even more important, particularly for providers already managing demanding patient loads. There is a quota attached to this role, and I intend to hit it by being useful to clinicians and keeping the patient at the center. Eighteen months as a missionary taught me not to flinch at a closed door. I'm coming in without a pharma background. I know that's the gap, and I'd rather be coached hard than pretend otherwise. I played competitive basketball most of my life, so I know the difference between a team pulling in the same direction and people protecting their own numbers. I want to be the partner people are glad they got.

startStories.title: Sales Performance & Brand KPIs
startStories.teaser: "Deliver sales performance, brand KPIs, financial targets, marketing objectives..."
startStories.body:
At Vivint, I wasn't in the field. I was setting the targets the field reps had to hit. I built the executive forecasting models and diagnosed the performance gaps that became the team's strategic goals, then presented a business case to senior leadership that secured a $2M+ revenue expansion opportunity.

At Goldman Sachs, hitting the number was more literal: 10 to 20 complex transactions a week with zero-defect accuracy, often in a 70 plus hour workweek, with no room for error. I finished with 100% retention and zero escalations.

startStories.title: Pre-Call Planning & Post-Call Evaluation
startStories.teaser: "Create pre-call plan objectives and execute post-call evaluation..."
startStories.body:
As a volunteer representative across Nebraska, Iowa, and South Dakota, I built this process from scratch. Before every visit, I wrote a specific pre-call plan objective. After every visit, I ran a post-call evaluation, tracked in a CRM pipeline, capturing objections so I could handle them better next time. More than half my new pipeline came from referrals, and I hit my weekly numbers 12 weeks straight.

At Goldman Sachs, when a senior client pushed back on a contract term, I found the misread myself, got internal leadership aligned, and closed the objection out before it became a lost account.

startStories.title: Trusted Relationships & Win-Win Agreements
startStories.teaser: "Serve customer needs, expectations and challenges to build trusted customer relationships..."
startStories.body:
A community leader in my mission territory was the gatekeeper to an entire network, and he hadn't worked with a missionary in years. Everyone before me said not to bother. Instead of pushing him, I got to know his wife over weekly lunches, learned he missed playing soccer, and started a recurring community game he only had to show up to. He went from ignoring us to mobilizing his whole network on our behalf.

Resistance is usually just information about what someone actually values.

At Goldman Sachs, I managed 20+ institutional relationships with senior decision makers who had every option available to them and no obligation to stay loyal. Reading what each one needed and delivering it is what kept them.

startStories.title: Call Planning & Territory Coverage
startStories.teaser: "Develop and execute a call plan that achieves set call metrics and optimizes coverage and frequency..."
startStories.body:
Across a 3-state mission territory, I built a weekly rhythm of visits, follow-ups, and referrals instead of relying entirely on cold outreach, planning each week around who to see and how often.

At 1-800 Contacts, I built a nationwide heat map across 42,000+ U.S. ZIP codes to identify exactly where spend and coverage should be concentrated for maximum reach.

startStories.title: Market & Clinical Intelligence
startStories.teaser: "Continuously build understanding on customer needs, territory market landscape, competitors..."
startStories.body:
At Vivint, I used SQL, Snowflake, and Python to identify territory-level performance gaps and help leadership understand what was driving them.

At 1-800 Contacts, I didn't just build the market intelligence. I shared it, training the Analytics Team on the ZIP code targeting framework I built.

My clinical foundation comes from my EMT training, including hands-on experience in the psychiatric section of the ER and coursework in psychiatric emergency response and pharmacology fundamentals.

startStories.title: Identifying & Developing Speakers and Advocates
startStories.teaser: "Identify, develop, and maintain disease state experts and speakers/advocates..."
startStories.body:
During my 18 months as a Spanish-speaking volunteer representative, one community leader was the gatekeeper to an entire network, and he hadn't worked with a missionary in years. Everyone before me said not to bother. So I got to know his wife first, over weekly lunches, and learned he missed playing soccer with a group he'd lost touch with. I started a recurring community game and told him all he had to do was show up. He came, and over time he went from ignoring us to making referrals and mobilizing his whole network.

The lesson has stayed with me: identify the people who influence a community, understand what matters to them, and earn the relationship before asking for anything.

experience.title: Licensed Emergency Medical Technician
experience.body:
Top 5% of cohort, delivering hands-on clinical support across the emergency room, trauma bay, ambulance, and in-transit care.

I provided direct patient care in the emergency department's dedicated psychiatric section and completed training in psychiatric emergency response and pharmacology fundamentals. I assisted an ER physician during a high-acuity emergency tracheotomy and supported emergency air transport intake from rooftop helipad arrival through trauma bay admission, working alongside physicians, nurses, EMTs, firefighters, and trauma teams. That experience gave me an early understanding of the pace, pressure, and clinical realities providers face in psychiatric care.

experience.title: Global Markets Analyst — Client Relationships & Syndicated Loan Operations
experience.body:
Managed 20+ institutional relationships across multi-million dollar syndicated loan portfolios, completing 10 to 20 complex transactions weekly with zero-defect accuracy in a 70 plus hour workweek.

I read through 100 to 250-page loan agreements so I could answer a client's question before they thought to ask it, finishing with 100% retention and zero escalations. When one client pushed back on a contract term, I found the misread myself and got internal leadership aligned to keep the account. Learning dense, unfamiliar contracts taught me how to get fluent in complex information quickly. I would bring that same approach to mechanism of action, payer language, and competitive data in a therapeutic area.

experience.title: Business Operations Analyst
experience.body:
Diagnosed territory-level performance gaps and built executive forecasting models in SQL, Snowflake, and Python to translate complex data into clear, board-aligned growth strategy.

I presented a C-suite business case that secured a $2M+ revenue expansion opportunity and directly influenced how leadership allocated resources. It taught me to look beyond the number and understand what is actually driving performance.

experience.title: Financial Analyst Intern
experience.body:
Built a nationwide marketing performance heat map across 42,000+ U.S. ZIP codes to identify underperforming spend, market segments, and high-potential growth territories, then trained the Analytics Team on the framework I built.

I taught myself SQL from scratch to build it. That experience taught me how to learn an unfamiliar market quickly and turn what I learn into something the broader team can use.

experience.title: Executive Director (Volunteer) — BYU Chapter
experience.body:
Presided over a 5-person leadership team overseeing 100+ volunteer advocates supporting court-involved children in a high-stakes judicial environment.

Many of the children I advocated for were navigating serious mental health needs, which gave me an early, first-hand understanding of what's at stake in psychiatric care. I built trusted relationships with judges, attorneys, families, and multidisciplinary stakeholders through emotionally intelligent communication. It taught me that earning trust often means understanding the needs of everyone involved, not just the person making the final decision.

experience.title: Full-Time Volunteer Representative — Nebraska, Iowa & South Dakota
experience.body:
Grew membership across a 3-state territory by identifying and developing influential community advocates who referred and influenced others, reducing reliance on cold outreach.

More than half of my new pipeline came from referrals, and I hit my weekly numbers 12 weeks straight while onboarding and mentoring a new representative. I wrote pre-call plan objectives and ran post-call evaluations through a CRM pipeline. I went in with classroom Spanish and came out fluent, using it every day for 18 months with hundreds of families and individuals. Eighteen months of hearing no and knocking on the next door anyway taught me that rejection is information, not a reason to slow down. That mindset still shapes how I approach territory coverage and follow-up.
